Hi Takashi — thanks, and glad the demo was useful. Looping in Marissa (privacy/legal) and Kim (infra) to respond with specifics. High-level answers first:

- Subprocessors: For a Japan pilot using our hosted inference, tokens traverse Redwood's hosted API front door (ingress in ap-northeast-1), are queued into our serving pool, and may use the following subprocessors: GCP (ap-northeast-1) for ephemeral compute, S3-compatible object store (regional), and DataDog (monitoring). I will confirm the exact hostnames and availability zones in the spreadsheet.

- DPA & transfers: Redwood's standard DPA references the EU SCCs (2021) where relevant and includes a UK IDTA addendum when contracts require it. For Japan-specific exports, we treat transfers similarly and rely on our contractual safeguards plus technical controls; Marissa will confirm which clause to reference for your procurement.

- TIA scoping: We will answer the spreadsheet. For KV cache: sessions are short-lived (ttl < 1 hour for pilot) and we do not persist prompt content beyond operational metrics unless customer opt-in for logging is enabled. All in-transit traffic is TLS 1.3.

We will aim to return a filled scoping sheet and a one-page attestation by Monday EOD JST.

Mina
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Takashi — Marissa here, Privacy Counsel. Quick clarifications while Kim fills the spreadsheet: 

1) Contractual safeguards: For Japan pilots where the customer requests explicit transfer language, we point customers to Section 7 of our DPA (Export Controls & Transfer Safeguards). That section cites the EU SCCs (controller-to-processor) and includes a selectable UK IDTA addendum for UK entities. For non-EU/non-UK customers we provide the same standard safeguards plus our technical controls; if Tokyo Meds requires a standalone Japan-specific addendum, we can discuss a narrow one for the pilot (limited to the pilot dataset, timeboxed).

2) Subprocessor attestation: We can provide a dated attestation listing subprocessors that will process pilot data. The attestation will include region/zone, retention assumptions (pilot: ephemeral), and a confirmation that we do not use US-based analytics on raw prompt text unless explicitly enabled.

3) Evidence & timing: We can produce the attestation + redacted subprocessor mapping and the filled TIA scoping sheet by Monday, but DocuSign countersignatures and procurement reviews may add 3–5 business days if Tokyo Meds needs it in execution form.

Please confirm whether you need the attestation on company letterhead (we can do that) or an inline PDF will suffice.

Thanks,

Takashi / team — technical notes and answers entered into the scoping sheet (attached as csv export). Highlights: 

- Ingress/egress: Pilot traffic will terminate in ap-northeast-1 (GCP) for low latency. No cross-region hop for inference tokens unless you opt into multi-region redundancy.
- KV cache: cache is per-session, stored in-memory on the serving instance; TTL set to 45 minutes for pilot. We do not write session-level content to long-term object storage unless logging enabled.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest for any persisted artifacts. Keys are managed in customer-visible KMS for Private deployments; for hosted pilots we use our KMS with strict key rotation and CMKs for enterprise plans.
- Subprocessors referenced: gcp-apn1-compute.redwood (ephemeral compute), redwood-region-store-apn1 (object store), datadog-monitoring (metrics only). See Redwood_Subprocessors_May2028.csv for the full list and zones.

Attachment: Redwood_Subprocessors_May2028.csv (csv)

If you want, we can carve an execution-only TIA that only covers the pilot's ingest and inference flow and excludes analytics/metric exports. That would make procurement simpler.

-Kim
